subject: Orbis Health - interoperability benchmark ops & next steps
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Dunne <claire.dunne@orbishealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 May 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed test matrix (Orbis Health)

Claire — thanks again for the productive call earlier. Quick recap and a proposed ops plan so we can move to a hands-on comparison next week.

Summary of what we heard from Orbis:
- Primary use case: real-time clinical summarization + index searching (avg prompt 180-350 tokens, latency SLO ~200ms p95)
- Production concurrency target: steady 120 qps with spikes to 350 qps for short windows
- Regulatory note: logs retention & auditability are required; procurement will ask for SOC2 evidence

Proposed bench goals (what Redwood will run vs Hyperscaler endpoints you called out):
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec (steady-state), cold-start 95th, CPU/GPU util, cost-per-1M-tokens
- Tests: A/B single-token-stream vs batched (batch sizes: 1, 8, 32), sequence lengths {128,256,512}, concurrency sweep (1, 10, 50, 120, 350)
- Variants: lightweight quantized model vs fp16 baseline; KV cache ON/OFF for chat flows

Operational asks from Orbis to run a fair comparison:
1) Access to the sample prompts (or a 50-line prompt set) and a representative document index
2) A short live window for pointer to your Hyperscaler endpoints + any rate limits we should respect
3) Contact from your procurement/security folks for SOC2 artifact requests

Attachments: initial_bench_matrix.xlsx (test matrix), redwood-inference-onepager.pdf (short differentiators)

Next steps I propose:
- You share sample prompts & hyperscaler endpoint details by EOD Friday (May 11)
- Redwood SE bench run starting Mon May 13, with a short interim sync on Wed May 15 to review preliminary p95 numbers
- Joint review on Fri May 17 to align on production roll plan if results look good

Ben/Jonas — I left the technical knobs we should pin below. Happy to adjust.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen

Thanks, Stephanie — this looks good and aligned with what we discussed. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- We can provide a 75-line prompt set and a redacted index dump (small) by Friday. Will that be sufficient?

Also, curious about the cold-start numbers you mentioned — can Redwood capture a warm vs cold distinction in a short run? We need that for orchestration decisions.

Claire / team — quick technical notes from the SE side so the bench is apples-to-apples:

- Cold vs warm: we can run explicit cold runs by restarting the instance between trace runs and measuring first-request p95/p99. We'll include both cold and steady-state measurements.
- Cache config: for chat-style flows we'll run two sets: KV-cache ON (to show typical app perf) and KV-cache OFF (to show raw model latency). For fairness vs the hyperscaler please confirm if caching is enabled on their side; if unknown, we'll default to "off" for the comparative baseline and run a cached run for a separate comparison.
- Quantization: default fp16 baseline, plus 4-bit quantized variant (if your workload tolerates it). Quantized runs will get separate columns in the results so you can inspect quality vs cost.
- Batching & concurrency: our runner will sweep batch sizes 1/8/32 and concurrency levels 1/10/50/120/350 as Stephanie listed. We'll also capture tokens/sec at steady-state for each config.

Stub attachment: se-sample-request.json (small JSON showing our runner payload format).

Logistics: Stephanie — I can start the runs as soon as Claire shares the prompt set and the hyperscaler endpoints. If procurement needs a secure S3 presigned transfer, flag it and we'll coordinate.

-ben

Appreciate the quick confirmations. Final agreed ops plan below so everyone has the same expectation: 

1) Orbis to provide: prompt set + redacted index + hyperscaler endpoint + read-only key by EOD Friday (May 11) — Claire, you indicated this is doable.
2) Procurement (purchasing@orbishealth.com): Redwood will provide SOC2 Type II PDF and a short vendor questionnaire. We will share a presigned S3 link for any log artifacts you request.
3) Redwood SE plan: bench starts Mon May 13 (Ben to run). Initial interim review Wed May 15 (30m) to go over p95 results. Final technical review Fri May 17.
4) Measurement & pass/fail acceptance criteria (agreed): p95 < 220ms on steady-state for the primary model variant OR tokens/sec >= 12k at 120 qps (for 256-token sequences) OR cost-per-1M-tokens less than current hyperscaler baseline (we'll report all three).

I'll book the Wed and Fri review slots and share calendar invites (separate). If anything above needs to change, flag now so Ben can adjust runner configs.

Thanks all — looking forward to getting hands-on.
